newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian interest rates plummet after budget.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian interest rates plummet after budget.

text.p: Interest rates have fallen sharply in Nigeria 10 days after the military government unveiled the fiscal 1997 budget that promises to inject money into the system, bankers said on Thursday.
"Both lending and deposits rates are at their lowest levels for three years because the system is very liquid," said a spokesman for the Money Market Association of Nigeria (MMAN).
Lending rates have fallen to around 12 percent from 18 before the budget.
"Borrowing rates may even go down unless there is renewed demand for credit because at the moment business is still dull," said the MMAN spokesman.
Deposit rates are already in single digits. Some banks were on Thursday offering as low as seven percent compared to 15-16 percent before the budget.
Bankers said much of the new money in the system were deposits from government agencies who now have to open accounts with commercial banks.

Under new rules announced in the budget and which take effect from January 1, 1997, the central bank is relieved of all retail banking and while it would continue to bank federal government funds, accounts of state firms and ministries are to be transferred to commercial and merchant banks.
"Government agencies have six months to do this transfer and some are already doing so," said one banker.

The banks were already liquid following large injections by the Petroleum Trust Fund (PTF), set up by the government to utilise for the common good money realised from a fourfold increase in pump prices in October 1994.
PTF is set to spend 30 billion naira this year, about the same as last year on projects ranging from road rehabilitation to supply of drugs to cash-strapped public hospitals.
The government in the budget also voted to pay off debts owed local commercial banks by state government amounting to three billion naira.
Bankers said the outlook was for large inflow of funds.

"The massive liquidity in the system will bring down interest rates, both on the deposit and lending sides," said Tayo Aderinokun, deputy managing director of Guaranty Trust Bank at a post-budget seminar in Lagos on Wednesday.
